correctness.rationale: Exact neighbor counts imply a three-branch even-degree and four-branch odd-degree population rule. Even states are resolved by the balanced-vector involution; for odd n the six population-class representatives are exhaustive under exchange/complement symmetries and prove F^5=F^3. Inclusion–exclusion yields the labelled fixed/orbit/basin formulas, with n=1,2,3 separated. An independent explicit-neighbor simulator covered every labelled configuration for n=1..7, and a four-original-pair-type multinomial checker covered all pair profiles for n=1..50; both agreed. The proof, not finite checks, establishes arbitrary n.

value.rationale: The graph family is a canonical perfect-matching deletion from complete bipartite networks; removing these edges changes local tie geometry. The exact formulas reveal a natural, previously non-implied parity fracture (one oscillatory orbit for all odd n versus exponentially many for even n), although both attract approximately half of initial states with sharply different asymptotic rates. The complete sharp transient classification and exact basin populations are motivated dynamical invariants, not arbitrary finite slices.
